review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions in Combinators/Helpers.lean (idleDir, moveLeftDir, readBackWrite, writeAndMove_readBack, idleDir_start, idleDir_right_of_start). I grepped the Turing-machine library for how idleDir and moveLeftDir are unfolded elsewhere. Helpers.lean has no @[simp] lemmas and no lemma for the off-start case of either direction function. The repeated `rw [idleDir, ite_eq_right h]` and `simp [idleDir, …]` unfoldings across files support the finding. I could not run Lean. findings.declaration: rev_idle_eq / reverseTM_copy_loop / reverseTM_emit_loop (idleDir, moveLeftDir off-start unfolding)
findings.excerpt: rw [writeAndMove_readBack t h, idleDir, ite_eq_right h, Tape.move]
findings.problem: The simp interface for `idleDir` and `moveLeftDir` lacks the canonical off-start lemmas. Helpers.lean only provides the start-symbol cases (`idleDir_start`, `idleDir_right_of_start`, `moveLeftDir_right_of_start`). To reduce `idleDir g` or `moveLeftDir g` when `g ≠ Γ.start`, every proof unfolds the definition and then rewrites with `ite_eq_right`. This file does it at lines 110, 140, 146, 209, 233 and 239. Other files repeat it with `simp [idleDir, hread, Tape.move]` and `rw [idleDir, ite_eq_right hh]`. A file-private copy, `idleDir_stay_of_ge_one`, exists in Union.lean. Unfolding the definition exposes an `if` on `Γ`-equality instead of a normal form, so `simp` cannot reduce `idleDir c.input.read` to `.stay` from a hypothesis `c.input.read ≠ Γ.start` without a case-specific unfold.
findings.proposed_change: In Helpers.lean, next to `idleDir_right_of_start`, add `theorem idleDir_of_ne_start {g : Γ} (h : g ≠ Γ.start) : idleDir g = Dir3.stay` and `theorem moveLeftDir_of_ne_start {g : Γ} (h : g ≠ Γ.start) : moveLeftDir g = Dir3.left`. Prove them by `simp [idleDir, h]` or `if_neg h`. Mark them `@[simp]` so that, with `h` in the simp set, `idleDir`/`moveLeftDir` reduce without being unfolded. Both are conditional on a hypothesis that is already discharged by assumption, so there is no looping risk. Then replace the `rw [idleDir, ite_eq_right …]` and `rw [moveLeftDir, ite_eq_right …]` sequences here with `rw [idleDir_of_ne_start h]` or `simp [h]`. Keep `idleDir_start` and `moveLeftDir_start` as the start-symbol cases, so the two cases are complementary and do not compete.
findings.benefit: The `if` encoding is kept out of the proofs, and the same two lemmas serve this file, ParkAll, CopyOutput, Subroutines/Internal and the other users. Proofs state the intent (an off-start head idles or moves left) instead of unfolding and chasing `ite`. Definitions can be changed later without touching every proof.

findings.excerpt:
rw [moveLeftDir, ite_eq_right hwne]
        exact writeAndMove_readBack _ hwne _
findings.problem: The `hwmove` fact says that writing back the symbol read and moving left (via `moveLeftDir`) is `Tape.move Dir3.left`. It is proved twice with the same `funext` / `Subsingleton.elim` / unfold-`moveLeftDir` / `ite_eq_right` script, once in each loop (also at lines 236–240). The simp set cannot do this step itself. `writeAndMove_readBack` is stated for `Dir3` arguments and is not simp. Nothing reduces `moveLeftDir t.read` for an off-start head, and the one-tape `fun i => …` shape needs a manual `funext`. After `simp only [TM.step, reverseTM, …]` the goal has the form `fun i => (c.work i).writeAndMove (readBackWrite …).toΓ (moveLeftDir …)`. The proof must then `rw [hwmove]` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma in Helpers.lean such as `theorem writeAndMove_readBack_moveLeftDir (t : Tape) (h : t.read ≠ Γ.start) : t.writeAndMove (readBackWrite t.read) (moveLeftDir t.read) = t.move Dir3.left`, and an analogous `idleDir` version for off-start heads. Prove them by `rw [moveLeftDir_of_ne_start h, writeAndMove_readBack t h]`. Mark them `@[simp]`, or at least use them via `simp only [...]`. Then the two `hwmove` blocks reduce to `funext i; simp [Subsingleton.elim i 0, hwne]`, or are removed in favour of the lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes about 12 duplicated lines. It also lets the `TM.step` simp call finish the tape update directly instead of via a hand-built `hwmove` equation and a later `rw`. Other machines with the same idle or rewind pattern can reuse it.
